stories.title_orig: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
stories.summary_orig: Low-bit quantization reduces the inference cost of LLM agents but can compromise task success. Examining failed rollouts, we find that quantized agents overlook task requirements or environmental conditions, producing environment transitions that diverge from successful full-precision references. Correcting these behavioral divergences remains difficult: offline data may miss the student's failure contexts, while its own rollouts may provide few correct responses in those contexts. We introduce SteerDistill, a quantization-aware distillation method in which a full-precision teacher guides the student to revise failed responses and iteratively refines its guidance using feedback from student execution. This closed-loop teacher steering produces locally verified behavioral corrections. We internalize these corrections by training the student without guidance to match the steered student's predictions at corrected turns and the full-precision teacher's at other turns, enabling unassisted inference. Across five agentic benchmarks and three models, SteerDistill exceeds the strongest quantized baseline by 1.67--2.18 points in average score under W4A16 and stays within one point of BF16…

stories.title_orig: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks
stories.summary_orig: Mathematical supervision for language models is typically flattened into isolated problem-solution pairs, discarding the curricular organization and evidential structure of the original sources. We introduce TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence), a large-scale corpus that converts 2,118 textbooks spanning the core areas of university-level mathematics subjects into approximately 380K structured proof-supervision records while preserving chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and source provenance. Leveraging these structural signals, we explore curriculum learning across multiple mathematical subjects and characterize scaling patterns with supervision volume and source breadth. At full scale, fine-tuning on TOME-Math raises the unweighted mean score across our held-out evaluations and established public benchmarks by 16.7 percentage points over the base model, while exceeding all three public instruction-data baselines evaluated in aggregate. Our findings highlight structured textbooks as both a scalable source of mathematical supervision and an empirical framework for studying the impact of data organization on mathematical reasoning. stories.title_orig: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.summary_orig: Large language models (LLMs) draw on parametric knowledge and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to solve knowledge-intensive tasks. Yet problem solving in unfamiliar domains calls for tightly coupled knowledge acquisition and reasoning, beyond factual retrieval and aggregation or learning solely from a preassembled context. We study self-learning -- autonomously retrieving, studying, and applying knowledge from long-form reference materials on the fly. To investigate this capability, we formulate a textbook-based mathematical problem-solving task. LLMs must navigate textbook exposition, learn and apply relevant principles, and construct proofs for exercises, with reference solutions withheld. We introduce a BookNavigator interface to support this human-inspired study process and incentivize self-learning through reinforcement learning (RL) with fine-grained rewards. Experiments show that our method improves performance across in-domain and out-of-domain textbooks and subjects, raising Intern-S2-Preview-35B's overall proof accuracy from 51.5% to 79.5% and outperforming RL-trained textbook-free and fixed-retrieval baselines. These gains extend to complex long-context benchmarks…

stories.title_orig: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
stories.summary_orig: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support Web-based services that must balance response quality and inference cost across heterogeneous requests. Conventional routing selects one model per prompt, while fixed ensembles cannot adapt their composition and cost to individual requests. We introduce PISA, a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model router, and PISA-E, its extension to ensemble routing. At the core of both methods, PISA combines soft cluster memberships with model-specific predictors to estimate individual model capabilities. Building on these estimates, PISA-E jointly selects ensemble composition and cardinality under an explicit cost--quality preference that can be adjusted at inference time without retraining. A tractable ensemble-success surrogate and efficient candidate selection enable this extension without ensemble-specific training. Across four LLM routing benchmarks under in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions, PISA achieves the highest macro-average cost--performance hypervolume among the evaluated single-model routers in both settings. stories.title_orig: Reasoning Beyond Prediction: From Data-Driven to Causal Software Engineering
stories.summary_orig: Software engineering is an intellectually demanding, creative discipline that juggles a web of interdependent tasks to design, build, and assure the quality of increasingly complex systems. As our expectations from software soar—with demands spanning AI-driven products, pervasively distributed and cloud-native architectures, and deeply embedded cyber-physical environments—its complexity steadily increases. In response, a new wave of co-engineering methods and tools, fueled by deep learning, has emerged to augment the process, enhancing automation and decision support. Yet, these advances remain far from delivering the kind of intelligent support that modern software development demands. We call for a new paradigm of human-machine cooperation—one where machines don’t just automate routine tasks or predict from learned patterns, but actively amplify engineers’ reasoning through the lens of causation . As software becomes smarter, a smarter support is needed.

stories.title_orig: GTAGym: AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
stories.summary_orig: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. stories.title_orig: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
stories.summary_orig: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that neural networks are converging toward similar representation spaces. As language models become more capable, their representations are aligning with those of vision models. However, recent work has questioned whether this trend continues to hold for newer language models. Moreover, it has been shown that representation similarity metrics can be confounded by model depth and width, requiring appropriate baselines for interpretation. In this work, we first investigate where alignment emerges between unimodal models across model layers and representation dimensions. Next, we find that the PRH capability-alignment trend persists for newer models as long as the captions are sufficiently clean and informative. Finally, we contextualize cross-modal alignment, introducing unimodal and multimodal baselines on various datasets. Our results show that the cross-modal representational alignment of unimodal models can surpass that of explicitly aligned vision-language models, but remains substantially behind the alignment observed for models of the same modality. Code is available at https://github.com/ExplainableML/prh-closer-look.

stories.title_orig: Subliminal Learning in Vision-Language Models
stories.summary_orig: Subliminal learning is a phenomenon in large language models (LLMs) where a teacher passes a hidden preference to a student through training data unrelated to that preference. We study whether subliminal learning also occurs in vision-language models (VLMs). We finetune a teacher VLM to prefer a specific animal or facial attribute and use a control teacher from the same base model. Both teachers generate numbers for an unrelated visual task involving geometric shapes. Two students initialized from the same base VLM are finetuned on the same images, using numbers generated by either the biased or control teacher. Across VLMs ranging from 2B to 7B parameters, we find that both animal and facial preferences can transfer through this unrelated task. Students trained on biased-teacher outputs select the target more often than control students, with a difference of up to sim10 percentage points in the animal preference task. Transfer can become stronger with more training data and varies with the target preference, model, and how the numbers are generated. Beyond preferences, we show that the biased student's explanations use more of the same words and phrases as the biased teacher's…

stories.title_orig: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading of External Content for AI Agents
stories.summary_orig: Web-facing AI agents repeatedly access webpages, documents, repositories, and tool responses, yet reading interfaces often expose entire objects when only sparse evidence is needed. This over-reading increases token and latency costs and can dilute relevant evidence. We present SparseRead, a reusable reading control layer that governs content admission without modifying the agent model. Its Read Intent Protocol tracks evolving needs and source coverage; Adaptive Reader Backends select how evidence is located and exposed; and the Budgeted Read Gate bounds cumulative raw exposure per episode with faithful full-view fallback. A unified Reader interface supports interchangeable evidence acquisition across heterogeneous resources. Across six models, including Claude Opus 5, and five scenarios, SparseRead reduces total tokens by up to 92.9% and wall time by up to 89.0%, preserving or improving task quality in 97% settings. On Web deep-search tasks, it reduces tokens by 31.0--43.0% and task completion time by 23.0--37.0%. Ablations validate the three designs, while integration with three agent frameworks demonstrates portability.
stories.title_vi: Đọc ít hơn, giải quyết nhiều hơn: Token-Đọc thưa hiệu quả nội dung bên ngoài cho AI Agents
stories.summary_vi: AI hướng web agents liên tục truy cập các trang web, tài liệu, kho lưu trữ và phản hồi của công cụ, nhưng các giao diện đọc thường hiển thị toàn bộ đối tượng trong khi chỉ cần một số ít bằng chứng. Việc đọc quá mức này làm tăng token và chi phí độ trễ, đồng thời có thể làm giảm bớt các bằng chứng liên quan. Chúng tôi xin giới thiệu SparseRead, một lớp kiểm soát đọc có thể tái sử dụng, điều chỉnh việc tiếp nhận nội dung mà không cần sửa đổi mô hình agent.

reasons: từ khóa Mô hình ngôn ngữ +2

stories.title_orig: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
stories.summary_orig: Agentic workloads are a major source of LLM inference demand. Existing prefill--decode (PD) disaggregated serving systems offer limited flexibility for runtime adaptation of compute allocation and KV cache management, and rely on coarse signals that only partly capture the diverse and dynamic agent workload. These limitations lead to load imbalance between prefill and decode nodes and eviction of KV caches that agents will reuse. We present Evolving Infra, an agent-adaptive serving framework that adapts compute allocation to agent workloads and KV cache management to agent context management at runtime. We decouple compute allocation from key--value (KV) cache management, allowing nodes to switch efficiently between prefill and decode. Building on this design, an online planner matches the PD split to workload composition, while an agent-aware distributed KV manager guides cache eviction and transfer with signals from agent context management. Across coding, math, and computer-use tasks with GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 on up to 256 GB300 GPUs, Evolving Infra reduces mean end-to-end request latency and P95 TTFT by up to 4.1x and 14x over Dynamo, NVIDIA's production framework.
stories.title_vi: Cơ sở hạ tầng đang phát triển: Agent-Phục vụ LLM thích ứng ở quy mô lớn
stories.summary_vi: Các khối lượng công việc Agentic là một nguồn chính của nhu cầu suy luận LLM. Các hệ thống phục vụ phân tách điền trước - giải mã (PD) hiện có cung cấp khả năng linh hoạt hạn chế để điều chỉnh việc phân bổ tính toán và quản lý bộ nhớ đệm KV khi đang chạy, đồng thời dựa vào các tín hiệu thô chỉ nắm bắt được một phần khối lượng công việc agent đa dạng và năng động. Những hạn chế này dẫn đến tình trạng mất cân bằng tải giữa các nút điền trước và giải mã, cũng như việc xóa các bộ nhớ đệm KV mà agents sẽ tái sử dụng.

stories.title_orig: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
stories.summary_orig: We present FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control. FAME-QP combines constraint-dependent operator representations with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs, automatically selecting the execution configuration through device calibration and problem-specific timing. It probes a cached operator bank to select the initial penalty and updates operators lazily when problem matrices change. Numerical benchmarks and simulated humanoid and quadrotor control experiments demonstrate reduced latency relative to competing GPU solvers while maintaining solution accuracy and control performance.
stories.title_vi: FAME-QP: Bộ giải lập trình bậc hai được tăng tốc GPU cho điều khiển dự đoán mô hình thời gian thực
stories.summary_vi: Chúng tôi xin giới thiệu FAME-QP, một trình giải được tăng tốc bằng GPU dành cho các chương trình bậc hai dày đặc phát sinh trong điều khiển dự đoán mô hình tuyến tính. FAME-QP kết hợp các biểu diễn toán tử phụ thuộc vào ràng buộc với các phép lặp một và hai nhân được hợp nhất, được phát lại thông qua các đồ thị CUDA, tự động chọn cấu hình thực thi thông qua hiệu chuẩn thiết bị và thời gian cụ thể cho từng bài toán.

stories.title_orig: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
stories.summary_orig: Visual interaction models that support users during ongoing physical tasks require evaluation in closed loop, where assistant responses can change subsequent user behavior and task outcomes. Existing benchmarks largely rely on offline replay and therefore cannot capture these effects. We introduce Interactive Visual Gym, a framework for closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models through joint simulation of executable task environments and human users. We contribute three simulators that recreate everyday tasks and human-aligned action spaces across cooking, household manipulation, and mobile-interface domains, together with a persona-conditioned user simulation harness that collaborates with the assistant while incorporating controlled execution errors and other out-of-plan behaviors. We instantiate the framework as IVG-Bench, a benchmark with 315 interaction scenarios. Evaluating state-of-the-art VLMs as visual interaction models reveals substantial limitations: the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, completes only 53.4% of tasks within the time limit, exhibits significant weaknesses in factual grounding and actionable guidance, and is often too slow to…

stories.title_orig: SoftBank’s billion-dollar loss may have put a cap on AI’s natural gas ambitions

stories.title_vi: Ngày càng có nhiều nhà phát triển trò chơi bắt đầu sử dụng AI tạo sinh

stories.title_orig: Phota Labs uses AI to turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots
stories.summary_orig: Rather than giving consumers yet another photo-editing tool, Phota Labs aims to use advances in AI to automate the editing process so it’s easier for anyone to turn everyday moments into better photos.
stories.title_vi: Phota Labs sử dụng AI để biến những bức ảnh chụp hàng ngày thành những bức ảnh trông chuyên nghiệp
stories.summary_vi: Thay vì cung cấp cho người tiêu dùng một công cụ chỉnh sửa ảnh khác, Phota Labs hướng đến việc tận dụng những tiến bộ trong lĩnh vực AI để tự động hóa quy trình chỉnh sửa, giúp mọi người dễ dàng biến những khoảnh khắc thường nhật thành những bức ảnh đẹp hơn.
